questions.question: Anthrax is caused by:
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct, i.e. __**Bacteria**__.

__
 
• Anthrax is an infection caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis.
 
• Anthrax occurs in hoofed animals such as sheep, goats, etc.

 
 

 **Anthrax**__
 
 

 Causative Agent
 **Bacillus anthracis**
 
 

 Mode of Acquiring
 The infection is contracted through breathing in or ingesting bacterial spores. The spores can also enter the body through the skin. These spores can be found in soil and in domestic and wild animals.
 
 

 Affects
 The part of the body affected depends on how the spore enters the body (food, skin, inhaling).
 
 

 Symptoms
 
 
**Through skin (Cutaneous)**

 
 
• Small blisters and bumps
 
• Painless skin ulcer with a black center
 
• Swelling around sores
 

 
**Through inhalation**

 
 
• Fever, chills, sweating
 
• Chest discomfort, shortness of breath, and cough
 
• Dizziness, fatigue, and headache
 
• Nausea and vomiting
 

 
**Through food (Gastrointestinal)**

 
 
• Stomach pain and swelling
 
• Diarrhea (bloody), nausea, vomiting
 
• Swelling of neck and neck glands

questions.question: In which Congress Session, was the demand for 'Purna Swaraj' adopted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Lahore **Session__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Lahore Session-**__

 __
 
• The Indian National Congress, on 19 December 1929, passed ‘Purna Swaraj’ means total independence resolution at its Lahore session*.*
 
• In the same session,** Jawaharlal Nehru was elected as president of Congress**.
 
• It was announced publically on 26 January 1930.
 
• Nehru marched to the banks of Ravi with the Congress members and they took an oath not to rest until Purna Swaraj was achieved.
 
• On December 21, 1929, the Tiranga (tricolour) flag was unfurled.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Note:**

 
• The first Independence Day **(as Purna swaraj) **was celebrated on** January 26, 1930.**
 
• **Surat Session-**
 
 
• The 1907 Surat session was popularly known as **Surat Split** as the Congress split into two groups. i.e. Extremists and Moderates.
 
• It was presided by Moderate leader **RasBehari Ghosh**.
 
 
 
• **Kanpur Session-**
 
 
• In 1925, the Congress session was held in Kanpur and it was presided by Sarojini Naidu.
 
• **Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman Congress President**.
 
 
 
• **Karachi Session-**
 
 
• The Karachi session of INC was presided over by** Sardar Vallabbhai Patel in the year 1931**.
 
• The session approved the** Gandhi-Irwin Pact and passed** a resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy.

questions.question: Which act of British Parliament transferred the powers of the East India Company to British Crown?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct, i.e. __**Govt of India Act, 1858**__.

__
 
• In** ****August 1858 Govt of India Act,**__** **the **British Parliament** passed an Act that put an end to the rule of the Company. The control of the British Government in India was transferred to the British Crown. It took place due to the **Revolt of 1857**. 
 
• It provided absolute (British) imperial control over India without any popular participation in the administration of the country.
 
• All the authority for the governance of India was vested in the Governor-General in Council who was responsible to the Secretary of State.
 
• The Secretary of State was ultimately responsible for the British Parliament.
 
• The power was transferred from the **Company** to the **British Crown**.
 
• The **Governor-General** was made the **Viceroy** of India.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers drains into the Bay of Bengal?
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, i.e. __**Krishna**__.

The Indian rivers that flow into the Bay of Bengal include** __Krishna__, Kaveri, Ganga, **and the** Godavari**.

__
 
• **Krishna-**__

 
 
• The Krishna River is a peninsular river that rises from a spring near Mahabaleshwar and flows for about 1400 km and reaches the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Tungabhadra, the Koyana, the Ghatprabha, the Musi and the Bhima are some of its tributaries.
 
• Its drainage basin is shared by Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Some of the other major peninsular rivers which flow eastwards and drain into the Bay of Bengal are the Mahanadi, the Godavari, the Krishna, and the Kaveri.
 
• **Nagarjuna Sagar Dam **was built across the** Krishna river **at Nagarjuna Sagar where the river is forming a boundary between Nalgonda district of Telangana state and Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh state in India.
 
 

**Extra facts:**

 
• **The Narmada-**

 
 
• River Narmada, the** fifth largest river in India**, with a river flow** length of 1312 km** originates from** Amarkantak in Shahdol district of Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The Narmada flows westward and after passing through Madhya Pradesh, Gujrat and Maharashtra.
 
• it drains into the** Arabian Sea **near the Gulf of Cambay.
 
 
 
• **Sutlej-**
 
 
• The Sutlej River flows in India as well as** Pakistan**.
 
• The Sutlej River** originates from Rakshatsal near the Mansarovar Lake** with an elevation of 4555 meters where its local name is Logchen Khambao.
 
• The total length of this river is** 1500 km**.
 
• **This river flows in a length of 1050 km in India.**
 
• The tributaries of this river are** Spiti, Baspa**.
 
 
 
• **Note:** Narmada, Tapi, Sutlej drains into the Arabian sea.

questions.question: With reference to the development of a country, which of the following countries is associated to the Gross National Happiness?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Bhutan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In most countries including India, GDP (gross domestic product) is considered as the measure of growth. But** ****Bhutan**__ is a country where** **__**GNH**__** ****(gross national happiness)** means gross national well-being.
 
• Bhutan has outright rejected** GDP since 1971** to measure growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• A new approach was adopted here which measures prosperity under the formal principle of **gross national prosperity.**
 
• It encompasses the natural environment as well as the spiritual, physical, social and environmental health of the people.
 
• The basis of making its index is to **promote equal social development, cultural conservation, environmental protection, and good governance**.

questions.question: Which Central agency issues currency notes on behalf of Central Government?
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, i.e. __**Reserve Bank of India**__. 

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India__ (RBI) **is India's highest monetary institution.
 
• RBI was** __established in 1935__ by the RBI Act 1934**.
 
• RBI- Foreign Reserve, bank of banks, acts as banker and debt controller of the Government of India.
 
• **It is also responsible for printing notes and managing the supply of money in the Indian economy**.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India has the monopoly of printing the currency in the country.
 
• It has the right to issue **all types of notes** except** one rupee note.**

**Note-**

 
• Currency notes and coins of** one rupee and lower denominations are issued by the Ministry of Finance**.
 
• Under the** Coinage Act, 1906,** the Government of India has the sole right to mint coins.
 
• According to** Section 24(1) of the RBI Act, 1934, **RBI is not entitled to issue banknote of denomination of value of one rupee.
 
• The currency note of** one rupee is issued by the Ministry of Finance **and **signed by the Finance Secretary of India**.

questions.question: Who conducts the elections of Lok Sabha in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Election Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__** About Lok Sabha-**__

__
 
• The First Lok Sabha was constituted on 13 April 1952 after India's first general election.
 
• First Session of this Lok Sabha commenced on 13 May 1952.
 
• The 1st Lok Sabha lasted its full tenure of five years and was dissolved on 4 April 1957.
 
• First Lok Sabha period - 13 April 1952- 4 April 1957
 
• First Lok Sabha **Speaker** - **Shri G.V. Mavalankar**
 
• **Present Lok Sabha Speaker-OM Birla.** 

**​About Election Commission of India-**__

 
• It was** **formed on **25 January 1950**.
 
• The **headquarters** of the **Election Commission** is in **New Delhi**.
 
• **The First** Chief Election Commissioner of India was** Sukumar Sen**.
 
• The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of** the Election Commission**.
 
• There are** three members** in the Election Commission which include** a Chief Election Commissioner **and** two election commissioners.**
 
• They are appointed **for 6 years **or can work only till the age of 65, whichever comes first.
 
• **Shri Sushil Chandra** is the** current Chief Election Commissioner of India**.
